newsitem.title: USA: Top Clinton aides meet to discuss Iraq moves.
newsitem.headline: Top Clinton aides meet to discuss Iraq moves.

text.p: President Bill Clinton's top national security advisers met at the White House on Friday and discussed the next move in the U.S. showdown with Iraq, officials said.

Clinton was not expected to participate in the talks, which included Secretary of State Warren Christopher and Defence Secretary William Perry. "There are some advisers here," Deputy White House Press Secretary Mary Ellen Glenn said.
The meeting was held as the United States ordered a buildup of its forces in the region in preparation for an expected military strike on Iraqi targets.
Glenn said the administration was holding "extensive consultations" with allies, who generally had offered tepid support for two earlier cruise missile strikes in Southern Iraq.

An armada of U.S. ships and assault planes were closing in on Iraq on Friday for what is expected to be a punishing bomb attack aimed at ending President Saddam Hussein's defiance of allied patrols of Iraqi air space.
